desc:
Fruit trees stand along an infinite number line. fruits[i] = [position, amount] says that position position holds amount fruits. The rows are sorted by position and all positions are different.

You start at startPos. One step moves you one unit to the left or to the right. You may take at most k steps in total. Whenever you stand on a position you collect all the fruit there (each position can be harvested only once). Return the maximum total amount of fruit you can collect.

fruits = [[2, 8], [6, 3], [8, 6]], startPos = 5, k = 4
walk right: 5 -> 6 -> 8 (3 steps) collects 3 + 6
result = 9
hints: Whatever you do, the set of positions you visit is one contiguous interval around the start. So the answer is the best interval you can afford.

To cover the interval from position L to R, starting at S, you go to the nearer end first and then sweep to the other: cost (R - L) + min(|S - L|, |S - R|) (when S lies outside the interval, this is also valid).

Slide a window over the fruit rows. For each right index, move the left index forward while the cost of covering [pos[left], pos[right]] exceeds k, and keep the best fruit sum of the window using a running total.
editorial: The visited positions always form an interval [L, R] that contains the start (or is reached from it). The cheapest way to harvest all of it is to walk to the closer endpoint first, then walk across to the other one, so the cost is (R - L) + min(|S - L|, |S - R|). Using other routes (e.g. zig-zagging) only costs more. It is enough to consider intervals whose endpoints are fruit positions, because shrinking an interval to its outermost fruits never hurts.

For the fruit window [left, right] this cost is non-decreasing in right and non-increasing in left, so a two-pointer sweep applies: add the amount at right, move left forward while the cost is above k (the window may become empty), and record the sum. Time O(n), space O(1).
solution:
def maxFruits(fruits, startPos, k):
    n = len(fruits)
    left = 0
    total = 0
    best = 0
    for right in range(n):
        total += fruits[right][1]
        while left <= right:
            lo = fruits[left][0]
            hi = fruits[right][0]
            cost = (hi - lo) + min(abs(startPos - lo), abs(startPos - hi))
            if cost <= k:
                break
            total -= fruits[left][1]
            left += 1
        best = max(best, total)
    return best
